I YOUR SHIP

1.1 The one rule

Keep moving. Everything else in this manual is detail.

You are a courier. The company is the largest employer in the galaxy and it has calculated, precisely, how replaceable you are. The floor is open in every direction and there are no walls to put your back against. A stationary courier is a solved problem.

1.2 Controls

Move with WASD or the arrow keys. You do not aim and you do not fire — your rack does that, continuously, at whatever it decides is worth shooting. Your entire job is where the ship is.

Hold SPACE to boost: about 1.85 times your normal speed while the tank lasts. The tank refills when you stop. It does not refill while you hold the key down on an empty tank, which is a thing every courier tries once.

1.3 What kills you, and what does not

Your hull is measured in pips. Contact with anything hostile costs one. There is no health bar and no healing item you can buy on the floor — a pip is gone until something specific gives it back.

Your shield absorbs a hit and then recharges after a pause. The pause restarts every time you are hit, so a swarm that touches you repeatedly is far more dangerous than one big hit. This is the whole reason for the one rule.

1.4 Running the tank dry

If you have requisitioned Vapor Recovery, emptying the boost tank vents it: a shockwave out to 190 units that shoves everything away and deals 42 damage at the centre, falling off to nothing at the edge. Bosses are too heavy to shove and ignore it entirely.

It is a panic valve you pay for by spending everything you had. Used deliberately, it is an escape.

II THE FIELD

2.1 A shift has a clock

The floor fills on a schedule. It is not published, but it is fixed: the same seed produces the same shift, every time, down to the last drone. Nothing on the floor is rolled at random behind your back.

2.2 Waves announce themselves

Ambient traffic is constant and grey. A wave is different — it arrives from one bearing, in one colour, and it tells you before it lands. The first one comes at 8 seconds and they continue on a 45-second beat after that, escalating in content rather than in frequency.

Grey means background. Colour means this is the wave. There is no interface element for this; the field itself is the readout.

A wave carries one type, or two. Never three. When it carries two, one of them is the problem and the other is the complication.

2.3 Gems are experience

Everything you kill drops one. Their colour and size are the same information told twice: green below 3, gold below 8, and white-hot above that. Bigger and brighter is worth more, and you should be able to tell across a crowded floor without stopping to look.

Collect enough and the company offers you a requisition. That is chapter three's problem.

III THE COMPANY

3.1 The workforce

The floor staff are not one enemy with a health bar that grows. They are distinct roles that arrive at authored moments, and each one is introduced alone before it is ever combined with anything else. If you are meeting something for the first time, it is meeting you on its own — that is deliberate.

3.2 The wheel

Four elements, in a cycle. Blaze beats Frost, Frost beats Shock, Shock beats Void, and Void beats Blaze. A strong hit does 1.5 times damage; a weak one does 0.66. Kinetic is neutral and is beaten by nothing.

3.3 Champions are a tool

An elemental champion is worth more attention than its health suggests, because of what happens when it dies. Every champion death effect targets the other enemies, not you:

Frost leaves a lingering slow field out to 150 units, lasting 5 seconds. Blaze ignites nearby enemies within 170. Shock stuns nearby enemies within 190 for 1.1 seconds. Void drags nearby enemies inward within 260, which is how you make a crowd into a target.

Kill the champion in the right place and the wave does some of your work. Kill it in the wrong place and you have simply killed a champion.

3.4 Management

There are 5 of them and they arrive in order. Each one is a different fight rather than a larger one, and each brings the arena with it.

BOSSES

SUPERVISOR 1
your shift has been flagged for review
REGIONAL MANAGER 2
this district is underperforming
DIRECTOR OF THROUGHPUT 3
throughput is down. you are throughput
VP, LOGISTICS 4
the route has been optimized. against you
THE AUDITOR 5
your metrics have been escalated

IV REQUISITION

4.1 The draft

Level up and the company offers you a choice of requisitions. You take one. You do not take the others, and that is the entire design — a draft you cannot lose is not a choice.

4.2 Ordnance

Your rack fires by itself, so a weapon is a decision about coverage and behaviour, not about aim. There are 16 of them.

WEAPONS

Pulse Array Kinetic · shot
Rapid light bolts. Standard issue — like you.
Flak Spread Kinetic · spread
A short cone of pellets. Whatever gets close gets itemized.
Rail Lance Kinetic · shot
Slow, heavy, hits like a freight bill.

Lobbed ordnance pods. By the pallet. Spend the pallet, then reload.

A thin, fast stinger. The hole is regulation size.
Flame Jet Blaze · spread
A short, hot cone. On-site waste incineration. Blaze.
Cryo Jet Frost · shot
A wide, cold fan. Assets keep longer cold. Frost.
Tesla Coil Shock · shot
Fast crackling darts. The grid bills by the arc. Shock.

A slow, heavy collapsing round. It arrives when it arrives.

Two interns with jetpacks and a quota. More seats pending approval.
Fighter Bay Kinetic · hangar
A patrol of light interceptors on rotating shifts. Headcount grows as the paperwork clears.
Bomber Bay Kinetic · hangar
One bomber riding your flank with guided ordnance. Deliveries are scheduled, not discussed.

A slow escort that shells the thickest crowd from a distance. Coverage is billed by the acre.

A humming security perimeter. Anything that gets close is processed on the spot. No returns.
Retention Policy Kinetic · orbital
Charged assets kept on a short electric leash. They orbit you at all times; attrition is continuous and mandatory.
Solar Lance Blaze · beam
A charging plasma lance — it winds up, fires a burning burst, then recharges. Radiant compliance.

4.3 Forks and mergers

Rank a weapon far enough and it forks: two finals per base, and the fork changes what the weapon *is* rather than how big its number is. Mergers combine two racked weapons into something neither of them was. There are 12.

FUSIONS

HOSTILE TAKEOVER C-RAM Gatling, Saturation Swarm
The hose and the zip code, one department. Every tracer is ordnance now.
THE RESTRUCTURING Warhead, Total Write-Off
A singularity with a delivery area. The fallout files itself.
BLUE LINE EXPRESS Blue Line, Twin Gauge
A burning rail that reaches the next department over. And the one after that.
CERTIFIED STORM Certified Delivery, Sewing Machine
Four hundred summons a minute. Each one knows the address.
BREAKAGE POLICY Deep Freeze, Twin Gauge
Broken in transit. Claim denied.
CLASS ACTION Wall of Invoices, Certified Delivery
Every defendant served at once. The wells keep them in court.
TOTAL RETENTION Loss Prevention, Retention Policy
Nothing leaves the perimeter. The storm sees to it.
THE BLIZZARD OFFICE Blast Freezer, Wall of Invoices
Three freezers per volley, delivered wide. The whole floor moves at inventory speed.
THE ARC LEDGER Lance Array, Capacitor Bank
The rejection bounces. So does the invoice. Both compound.
THE CONSOLIDATION Slug Consolidator, Transcontinental
One car, one address, one line item. The whole line signs for it.
ARC FLASH Refinery Burn, Grid Overload
The grid faulted. The floor caught. Both are your fault.
THE FINAL NOTICE Transcontinental, Total Write-Off
Delivered to every address on the line. Then the line is repossessed.

V WHAT IS OUT THERE

5.1 The floor is not empty

Between the traffic there are things that were on the floor before you arrived and will be there after. None of them are aimed at you. All of them will kill you.

5.2 Black holes

A well does not chase you and does not need to. Inside its reach it simply pulls, and the pull is stronger than you expect. You will see it on your own hull first — motes tearing off toward the well, and the ship visibly crabbing against its own thrust. When you see that, you are already inside.

Most couriers die here, and they die because they did not believe it was dangerous.

5.3 Asteroids and cracked rocks

Ordinary rock is cover, and cover works: it stops enemy fire, and enemy fire does not curve.

A cracked rock is different. Break it and it pays a power moment — 6 kinds, one roll, never resources. Three are instant. Three are timed and run for 12 seconds, one at a time; a new one replaces whatever is running. All of your damage breaks rocks, including the passive and area sources, so you do not need to point anything at them.

5.4 Landmarks

There are places worth finding. They are rare on purpose and they will not appear next to you — the floor keeps them at least 1200 units out, and your odds improve by travelling, not by circling. Cover about 1500 units of real distance and the floor starts offering.

You get one ping when you are near. There is no permanent arrow, and there will not be one.

5.5 Objectives

A ring on the floor is an offer, and a dashed ring is an offer you have not accepted. Fly in and hold position to accept it; then hold the ring while its garrison converges on you. The garrison is elemental, it is stronger than the ambient floor, and it drops nothing at all — the payoff is the requisition at the end, not the bodies on the way.

You can decline. The ring decays on its own and the shift continues. Declining is a real option and sometimes the correct one.

6.3 Standing Directives

Directives are earned rewrites of the rules rather than bonuses. They change how a shift works.

DIRECTIVES

Just-In-Time Delivery Pull the trigger 15,000 times (lifetime).
No magazines. Guns never reload — and never hurry. Fire 20% slower, forever.
Zero Inventory Reach 60 clearance levels (lifetime).
Nothing drops. Kills bank XP directly at 85 cents on the dollar. The magnet is retired.
Hostile Workplace Dismiss 10 Supervisors (lifetime).
The shield generator is removed. Two extra hull pips, and contact injures the other party too.
Perpetual Motion Clause Survive 3 hours on the floor (lifetime).
The boost tank never empties. Standing still voids the shield warranty — it drains.
Single Vendor Agreement Process 25,000 units (lifetime).
After your first install, the draft only ever offers THAT weapon. Duplicates forever. One supplier.

6.4 The Hazard Pact

You can make a shift harder on purpose, and be paid more for it. The company is happy to accommodate this.

VII COLOPHON

7.1 Same seed, same shift

Fulfillment is deterministic. The same starting conditions produce the same run, every time — the same waves, on the same bearings, at the same second. The company does not believe in luck. Only in variance it has not yet priced.

7.2 The paperwork

This manual is generated from the shipped game's own data. Every figure in it — every radius, duration, count and multiplier — is exported from the build rather than transcribed, so it cannot quietly drift out of date while the sentences around it stay still.

Now clock in. Standard is expected.
